text.p: Following are the main stories in Slovenia's Thursday morning newspapers.
- The government raises highway tolls by 10 percent from September.

- Slovenia said it would file a complaint regarding the Cypriot court decision saying the court cannot rule in the case of division of money of former Yugoslavia which was transferred to the Cypriot branch of Yugoslav bank Beogradska Banka.
- Financial inspectors found various irregularities in the accounts of government ministries and state institutions that they checked this year.
- Due to necessary parliamentary procedures the parliament is not likely to pass the 1997 government budget proposal before November.
- Right-wing parties have not yet decided whether they will jointly name a candidate to stand against current president Milan Kucan at the presidential elections later this year.

- The largest claim according to the so-called denationalisation law, which obliges the state to return property confiscated after the second world war, is a request for the return of 26,826 hectares of forest.
- Heavy rain caused a lot of damage in the area of Zasavje, east of Ljubljana.
- Players of Ljubljana's basketball club Union Olimpija started training for the next season in Slovenia's health resort Zrece. The club came third in this year's Euroleague championship.
